os_version: 26, Apple silicon (arm64); macOS 26.7.2 on the macos-26 runner when spike S11 ran on 2026-11-16 (Xcode 26.6, Apple clang 21.0.0, SDK 26.5); the minor version of the first run of the Apple CI job is not known, the id of the probe line is macos-26-arm64 whatever it is
environment_detail: The GitHub-hosted runner macos-26 (an Apple silicon virtual machine of GitHub Actions, ADR 0018; the only Apple system of the project: no Mac is owned and the macOS virtual machines on the PC failed, ADR 0019). NOTHING WAS COMPILED OR RUN FOR THIS RECORD: the Apple CI job (T126, .github/workflows/apple.yml) has not run, and tools/build.py macos / ios targets and the Apple UIs were written without a Mac. The record stands for what the macos-modern and macos-legacy jobs are meant to do on it: build the Modern UI (Universal 2, deployment target macOS 11) and run it with --probe on macOS 26; compile the Legacy UI for x86_64 at -mmacosx-version-min=10.6 (validation/spikes.json S11 linked a program that way on this runner, which is the only fact measured here). Under the spec Clarifications (fifth session) the Apple UIs are verified only on this runner: floor builds (macOS 11 Modern, macOS 10.6 Legacy) are compiled, never run, and no platform record stands for macOS 11 or 10.6.
eol_source: validation/sources.json eol-apple-security: Apple patches the latest releases; the entries of 2026-11-09 read on 2026-11-12 patch macOS 15, 26 and 27, and the backend (loomora_is_eol) treats macOS 14 and below as end of life, so 26 is not.
release_date_source: General availability of macOS 26 Tahoe (2025-09-15), taken from the author's knowledge, not from a page re-read for this record; age_years = days from 2025-09-15 to 2026-11-16 divided by 365.25, rounded to 0.1.
floor_note: Not the floor of the macOS family (macOS 10.6 Snow Leopard, spec Clarifications, floors). It is the lowest platform that can be RUN under the fifth-session rule (the macos-26 runner, SC-002 read with it); the 10.6 floor is only compiled for, never run, and waits for a real old Mac (spike S2, T067).
